summary.text: 肉 is an indivisible pictograph depicting a piece of meat or animal flesh; its modern strokes should not be read as separate pictures.

formation.text: Pictographic: the whole graph depicts meat. The received Shuowen account describes it as 胾肉, a large piece of meat, and classifies the graph as pictographic; this does not by itself establish the date or earliest use of the graph.

history.text: 肉 is represented in oracle-bone, Chu manuscript, and Small Seal categories. The selected Small Seal image is a modern redraw of a seal-script form, not an ancient specimen. These materials do not give a detailed sequence of graphic changes or dates for individual examples.
The graph’s pictographic explanation does not determine the deeper history of the spoken word. Proposed accounts of that word’s origin remain unresolved.

uncertainties.text: The available material does not date individual specimens, establish the earliest attested use of the character’s senses, or provide a complete sequence of graphic changes. It also does not resolve proposed deeper etymologies of the spoken word.

senses.text: The received Shuowen account glosses 肉 as 胾肉, interpreted in its later annotation as a large piece of animal meat. Dictionary citations document uses for meat and bodily flesh, but do not establish their exact dates or which use came first.
A dictionary records 肉 for fruit pulp, with a citation from 齊民要術. The date and any development from the meat sense are unresolved.

senses.gloss: solid part of a perforated ring
senses.text: Dictionary explanations and citations record 肉 for the solid part of a perforated ring. They do not establish when this use arose or how it relates to the meat sense.
A dictionary records a use of 肉 for musical voice or timbre. Its date and any semantic path from the meat sense are unresolved.
In current Chinese, 肉 means meat or flesh; the supplied record gives the Mandarin reading ròu.

limitations.text: Dictionary citations do not establish the earliest attestation of these senses or their chronological and semantic relationships, so no development is asserted without a dated sequence.
The pictographic account concerns the graph and its depicted referent; it does not resolve the spoken word’s deeper etymology. Proposed comparisons remain unresolved.

overview.text: 肉 is a whole-picture character representing a piece of meat or animal flesh. Its strokes do not form a combination of smaller components.
